Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .20,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

sentences.text:
The petition averments in brief is that on 07.05.2022 at about 5.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his Motorcycle bearing Regn.No.KA-05-KQ-1207 from Bengaluru towards Somanahalli side, when reached near Udipalya Bus Stand, Bengaluru-Kanakapura main road,
Uttrahalli Hobali, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-53-F-0242 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle.

Due to which, he sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to BGS Hospital and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was doing Surgical item supplier work at Bio Space Technologies, J.P. Nagar, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has became permanent disablement.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus by its driver.
The respondent being the RC owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, respondent appeared before the tribunal and filed his written statement.

4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent is as under:
The respondent has filed counter to petition by denying the petition averments.
He has further disputed the manner of accident, age of injured and quantum of compensation claimed under different heads.

Further contended that as per information received by this respondent, on 07.05.2022 the driver of bus while doing his duty and driving the said bus of route No.213QA/1 from Gottagihalli Bus Stop to KR Market Bus Stop and when he was driving slowly and he was reached near Udipaly bus stop, at that time the petitioner i.e., a rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-KQ-1207 i.e., came in high speed and rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and due to uncontrollable high speed and he himself dashed front portion of the bus.
Further the driver of the bus was driving slowly and he did not cause alleged accident and hence, there is no negligence on the part of driver of BMTC Bus.
Further contended that the rider of motor cycle has not acquired effective driving license and at the time of accident deceased was not wearing ISI certified helmet.
Further contended that there is no negligence on the part of driver of BMTC bus.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.05.2022 at about 05.00 a.m., near Udipalya Bus Stand,
Kanakapura-Bengaluru Main Road, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA- Sri.Sharath.N vs The Managing Director on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137628526/
2 05-KQ-1207, due to the rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-53-F-0242 by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and Dr.Ramachandra examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed their side of evidence.

The driver in respondent corporation in Depo No.44 examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked on behalf of respondent and closed his side of evidence.
7.
I have heard arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.

The petitioner has contended that on 07.05.2022 at about 05.00 a.m., Near Udipalya bus stand, Kanakapura - Bengaluru Main Road, Uttarahalli Hobali, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru, he met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA- 53-F-0242 by its driver and he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-53-F-0242 by its driver, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1.
In his chief examination he has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus by its driver the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 & 2 FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.2 first information, one Sri.Arun Kumar, S/o.Ramamurthy has lodged a complaint with police on 07.05.2022.
After registering the case Police went near place of accident and drew up Mahazar as per Ex.P.3 by narrating the place of accident.

Ex.P.4 - IMV Report,
wherein mentioned that the damages caused to both the vehicles.
Ex . P.5
Wound certificate, it shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
After completion of investigation, the police have filed charge sheet at Ex.P.6 against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC.
In order to disprove the case of petitioner, the driver in Respondent Corporation examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked on his behalf.

Sri. Sharath.N vs The Managing Director on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137628526/
3 RW.1 deposed that he was on duty as driver in BMTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-53-F-242, route No.213QA/1 from Gottigehalli Bus stop to K.R.Market bus stop and when he reached Udipaly bus stop, at that time the rider of motor cycle came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and due to uncontrollable high speed and dashed front portion of bus and rider was solely responsible to said accident and there is no negligence on the part of driver of BMTC Bus.
The respondent has not examined the eye witness before the tribunal to prove their contention.
Only on the basis of the chief examination of RW.1, this tribunal cannot say that only due to negligence on the part of petitioner the accident occurred.
Except placing oral evidence, the respondent nothing placed before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-53-F-0242 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discussion one by one.

(i) Towards injury and pain and suffering:-
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he has sustained injuries and underwent surgery and discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced Wound Certificate, marked at Ex.P.5, which reveals that petitioner has sustained injuries and doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.7 - Discharge summary the doctor diagnozed that petitioner sustained post traumatic closed right mid shaft both bone leg fracture.
So, on perusal of records, the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner examined Dr.Ramachandra as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 & 16.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and he assessed the disability for right lower limb at 31.72% and to whole body at 15.86%.
By considering the injury, year of accident and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .55,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 - 24 Medical bills for .31,859/-, in Ex.P.8 - Bill No.24 advance bill, hence this tribunal has not considered this bill.
The respondents not rebutted the other medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .26,859/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.

4 (iii) Vehicle Repair bill:-

entities.text: Sharath.N vs The Managing Director on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner produced Ex.P.9 - Vehicle repair bill of Rs.21,000/-.
Except producing Ex.P.9, the petitioner not examined the author of Ex.P.9 and also in support of Ex.P.9, he has not produced any materials to show that his vehicle repaired in Sridevi VOC.
So, in the absence of cogent evidence, this tribunal not considered Ex.P.9.
Accordingly, petitioner is not entitle for compensation towards vehicle repair.
(iv) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of the records, the accident occurred on 07.05.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.

So,
during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P.7 issued by Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Bengaluru, wherein it shows that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 07.05.2022 to 18.05.2022 i.e., for a period of 12 days.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .400/- per day for 12 days to a sum of .4,800/- is just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(v) Towards Conveyance:

The petitioner is the resident of Somanahalli, Uttrahalli Hobali, Bengaluru South,
Bengaluru.
He has admitted for treatment at Hospital.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summary.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(vi) Towards loss of income during treatment:

The petitioner has contended that he was doing surgical item supplier work at Bio Space Technologies, J.P.Nagara,
Bengaluru and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.

In order to prove his income,
the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income, this tribunal will consider notional income.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have not attended his regular work at least for a period of 2 months.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2022 at .15,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.
Case on hand the petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove his income.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2022 treated as .15,500/- per month as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

By considering facts and circumstance of case the petitioner is entitled for .31,000/-
(15,500/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment period.

(vii) Towards Permanent Disability:
Sri.Sharath.N vs The Managing Director on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137628526/
5
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was inpatient at Hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Ramachandra working in Victoria as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained closed fracture mid shaft of tibia and fibula of right leg and underwent ORIF with MIPO done on 13.05.2022.
The doctor has assessed the disability and he assessed the disability for right lower limb at 31.72% and to whole body at 15.86%.
The doctor has produced documents at Ex.P.15 & 16 i.e., outpatient slip and two X-ray films.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.

Therefore, considering all these aspects,
the functional disability is assessed at 9%.

In order to prove age of the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.11 & 12 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card and driving license, wherein date of birth mentioned as 14.12.1996 and accident occurred on 07.05.2022, so the age of petitioner is 26 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and multiplier 17 is applicable as per Smt. Sarla Verma case.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence,
future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (15,500/- x 12) = .1,86,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (9% of prior annual income) .16,740/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 17 Loss of future earnings - (16,740/- x 17) = .2,84,580/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .2,84,580/-. under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(viii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day-today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(ix) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.2 has deposed that petitioner advised to undergo another operation for removal of implants from Tibia of Right leg.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .10,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

13. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Total compensation .4,32,239/-
14.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. So, the respondent being the R.C owner of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-53-F-0242 is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .4,32,239/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Thirty Two Thousand Two Hundred and Thirty Nine only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

Respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favor of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
